interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for the Aug-Sep period was 88% against a 95% target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts — a real but partial (7-point) shortfall in manual meter-read collection. This is consistent with some missed reads feeding estimate substitution, but the magnitude alone does not establish it explains the full doubling of dispute tickets.
CRM data for 2440 dispute tickets shows median response time 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both inside the 3.0-day SLA — ticket response handling is performing within target, not backlogged or slow.

Of 3025 disputed bills, 1785 (59%) carry an ACTUAL read type and 1240 (41%) carry an ESTIMATED read type — the majority of disputed bills were billed from an accepted read, not from estimate substitution. This caps at ~41% the share of the dispute surge that any estimate-substitution-driven mechanism (AMI export failure, field read handoff failure, field staffing shortage) can account for.

The billing-db tariff change log shows zero recorded tariff changes, meaning no tariff/rate-table modification can account for the wrong bills or dispute surge; this rules out tariff edits as a causal mechanism but leaves billing-processing errors on accepted (ACTUAL) reads otherwise unexplained.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a shortfall of three readers since July causes late routes and resulting estimated bills, offering a candidate mechanism consistent with the manual-read shortfall already seen in E-01. As a non-authoritative claim from a stakeholder with an incentive to attribute problems to staffing, it does not by itself explain the 59% of disputed bills that carry an ACTUAL read type (E-03).

This is an authoritative confirmation of the surge's timing and magnitude, but it says nothing about what is causing the wrong bills or whether tickets are mishandled.
